note: Greenhithe, Kent: Erebus and Terror drop down the Thames, 129 men aboard
Stromness, Orkney: last British anchorage; five men discharged home here and from the transport, leaving 129
Whalefish Islands, Disko Bay: stores taken out of the transport Barretto Junior, last letters home written 12 July (inferred from the Admiralty despatches)
Melville Bay, Baffin Bay: made fast to an iceberg waiting for a passage; last sighting by Europeans, the whalers Prince of Wales and Enterprise
Lancaster Sound (inferred: no record between Melville Bay and Gore's summary of the first season)
up Wellington Channel (Gore's record: 'ascended Wellington Channel to lat. 77 deg.'; the intermediate track is inferred)
head of Wellington Channel at latitude 77 N, the season's farthest north; turned back here
returned by the west side of Cornwallis Island and re-entered Barrow Strait by a new channel between Bathurst and Cornwallis (Gore's record; McClintock pp. 284-285). Route inferred
Beechey Island: secured for the winter of 1845-46. Three men died and were buried here
leave Beechey Island in the summer of 1846 (month inferred; no record survives of the departure)
south down Peel Sound (inferred: the only route consistent with the besetment position)
Franklin Strait, past the west coast of Boothia (inferred)
beset in the pack off the north-west coast of King William Island, lat 70 deg 05' N long 98 deg 23' W in Gore's record; about twelve miles from the north extreme of King William Land
the ships are deserted, five leagues NNW of Victory Point, after nineteen months beset
Victory Point: the 105 survivors land, and Crozier and Fitzjames leave the record
start for Back's Fish River; the track beyond this point is the death march, not the ships' route
